correctness.rationale: On mu=0, the exact s,d,z reduction forces every nontrivial two-cycle to satisfy d1=-d0 and sin(z0)=sin(z1)=-1/(2h). Exhausting the two sine-root classes gives all two-cycles. Exact products of 2x2 Jacobian blocks yield multipliers 1±q (same branch) or repeated 1+q (opposite branches), with the third multiplier zero. Exactly the cross-class cycles with charge displacement 2(theta+pi*n) can be sinks, and their strict condition is rho(theta+pi*n)<1. Integer counting proves N(h), asymptotics follow from theta~rho~2sqrt(h-1/2). The implicit-function theorem continues any finite selected set to small mu>0 because F^2-Id has invertible derivative at hyperbolic sinks. Symbolic and high-precision checks from check.py passed; numerical checks are not a substitute for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The primary article motivates multistability but supplies no quantitative primitive-period-two construction. The result is a natural complete classification of a dynamical invariant (hyperbolic prime-two sinks) at a canonical input boundary and proves, beyond that boundary, arbitrarily many coexisting open-basin attracting cycles at strictly positive gain. The exact coupling staircase, square-root accumulation and repeated Floquet multiplier provide analytical structure unavailable from the reported basin plots. It is not an arbitrary finite parameter sample or a restatement of basic local persistence.
